blocks.text: 完整的生产栈

inlines.text: 完整的生产栈

blocks.text: 自 llm-d 发布以来，项目一直聚焦于改进 AI 推理的五种重要方法：前缀缓存感知路由，将请求导向可能已持有其共享上下文的基础设施；KV 缓存卸载，通过在 GPU、CPU 和存储资源之间移动缓存信息来延长其有效寿命；批推理优化，将工作分组以便基础设施更高效地处理；预填充/解码分离，将读取提示词的工作与生成响应的工作分开；以及宽专家并行，将大型混合专家模型分布到众多加速器上。

blocks.text: 在 1.0 版本中，llm-d 已成熟为一个能够支持第 2 天运维的栈：即 AI 服务部署之后必须发生的一切。这包括服务具有竞争优先级的工作负载、管理不同的性能需求、保持效率、优先处理重要服务，以及让系统长期保持可靠。基准测试可以表明某项功能提升了吞吐量，但生产系统必须在流量变化、硬件故障、软件更新或不同用户争夺同一资源时仍持续提供这种性能。llm-d 1.0 的目标就是让各项技术在这些更不可预测的条件下协同工作。

blocks.text: 一个端点，多种工作类型

inlines.text: 一个端点，多种工作类型

blocks.text: llm-d 1.0 在已经让 llm-d 成为强大分布式推理工具的核心技术创新基础上进一步扩展，增强了对多租户服务质量、零停机运维和智能体感知服务的支持，以在常见的第 2 天生产运维中保持持续性能。企业 AI 服务可能通过同一端点接收来自人员和自主智能体的请求，但这些工作负载的行为方式不同。使用编码助手的人期望快速得到答案。智能体可能发送大量突发请求，在使用工具时暂停，然后返回进行下一轮模型调用。

blocks.text: 借助流控，llm-d 1.0 可以管理工作负载是共享同一硬件还是跨越多种加速器时的竞争优先级。流控、公平性和优先级排序有助于防止突发工作负载压垮对延迟敏感的服务。在需求很高时，系统可以更审慎地决定哪些请求应优先获得资源。请求还可以在多个轮次中保持绑定到适当的基础设施。这可以保持其前缀缓存处于热状态，提高先前处理过的上下文被复用而不是重新计算的机会。

blocks.text: 这对对话式助手很重要，但对智能体尤其有价值。智能体在执行任务时经常回到相同的代码、文档、指令和对话历史。前缀缓存感知路由会将每一轮发送到已经持有相关上下文的副本，而 KV 缓存卸载有助于在 GPU 内存受限时保留更多可复用信息。这就是生产就绪在实践中的样子：通过理解到达模型的工作并相应地管理基础设施，更有效、更具成本效益地提供模型服务。

blocks.text: Today at the PyTorch Conference North America, llm-d project contributors are announcing llm-d 1.0, a major milestone for open-source AI infrastructure. A Kubernetes-native distributed inference serving network, llm-d makes it possible to deploy inference stacks for any model, on any accelerator, in any cloud.

blocks.text: The release signals that llm-d has moved beyond demonstrating individual performance techniques and is ready to support the realities of production: sustained efficiency under many workloads, all while balancing service priorities amid growing demand. And with inference costs increasing, llm-d is meant to help bring model deployment in-house and deliver returns on AI investment.

blocks.text: A full production stack

inlines.text: A full production stack

blocks.text: Since llm-d launched, the project has focused on five important approaches to improving AI inference: prefix-cache-aware routing, which directs a request to infrastructure that may already hold its shared context; KV-cache offloading, which expands the useful life of cached information by moving it across GPU, CPU, and storage resources; batch inference optimization, which groups work so infrastructure can process it more efficiently; prefill/decode disaggregation, which separates the work of reading a prompt from the work of generating a response; and wide expert parallelism, which distributes large mixture-of-experts models across many accelerators.

blocks.text: These ideas are not new to version 1.0. What is new is the level of integration and operational maturity around them.

blocks.text: With version 1.0, llm-d has matured into a stack capable of supporting day 2 operations: everything that must happen after an AI service is deployed. That includes serving workloads with competing priorities, managing different performance requirements, maintaining efficiency, prioritizing important services, and keeping the system dependable over time. A benchmark can show that one feature improves throughput, but a production system must keep delivering that performance when traffic changes, hardware fails, software is updated, or different users compete for the same resources. llm-d 1.0 is about making the individual techniques work together under those less predictable conditions.

blocks.text: One endpoint, different kinds of work

inlines.text: One endpoint, different kinds of work

blocks.text: Expanding on the core technical innovations that have already made llm-d a powerful tool for distributed inference, llm-d 1.0 enhances support for multi-tenant quality of service, zero-downtime operations, and agent-aware serving, for sustained performance in common day 2 production operations. An enterprise AI service may receive requests from people and autonomous agents through the same endpoint, but those workloads behave differently. A person using a coding assistant expects a fast answer. An agent may send a large burst of requests, pause while using a tool, and then return for another round of model calls.

inlines.text: Expanding on the core technical innovations that have already made llm-d a powerful tool for distributed inference, llm-d 1.0 enhances support for multi-tenant quality of service, zero-downtime operations, and agent-aware serving, for sustained performance in common day 2 production operations. An enterprise AI service may receive requests from people and autonomous agents through the same endpoint, but those workloads behave differently. A person using a coding assistant expects a fast answer. An agent may send a large burst of requests, pause while using a tool, and then return for another round of model calls.

blocks.text: With flow control, llm-d 1.0 manages competing priorities whether workloads share the same hardware or span a mix of accelerators. Flow control, fairness, and prioritization help prevent bursty workloads from overwhelming latency-sensitive services. Under heavy demand, the system can make more deliberate decisions about which requests should receive resources first. Requests can also remain pinned to the appropriate infrastructure across multiple turns. That keeps their prefix caches warm, increasing the chance that previously processed context can be reused instead of calculated again.

blocks.text: This matters for conversational assistants, but it is especially valuable for agents. Agents frequently return to the same code, documents, instructions, and conversation history while carrying out a task. Prefix-cache-aware routing sends each turn toward a replica that already holds the relevant context, while KV-cache offloading helps preserve more of that reusable information when GPU memory becomes constrained. This is what production readiness looks like in practice: serving a model more effectively and more cost-effectively by understanding the work arriving at that model and managing infrastructure accordingly.

blocks.text: Improving AI ROI with better infrastructure

inlines.text: Improving AI ROI with better infrastructure

blocks.text: This production focus leads directly to the economics of AI. As AI moves into everyday business operations, inference has become a recurring expense. Agentic systems can increase that expense because a single assignment may involve many rounds of reasoning, tool use, evaluation, and revision. If every step requires a model to reread the same material, you’re repeatedly paying for work the system has already done.

blocks.text: In a recent test of an agentic coding workload, llm-d’s prefix-aware router captured 97% of the available cache reuse. By avoiding repeated computation and making more efficient use of existing hardware, techniques like this can reduce the cost of serving AI at scale. In another recent demonstration, IBM and Red Hat ran 3,000 software-engineering agents concurrently on a self-hosted deployment for 5 to 10 times less than the actual price of serving the same open model as a service.

blocks.text: When an organization operates its own infrastructure, the infrastructure becomes part of a cost structure that can be managed. By combining open-weight models with an open serving stack, llm-d gives organizations another option for controlling the relationship between AI consumption, infrastructure spending, and business value.

blocks.text: That also gives llm-d an important role in the broader open-source ecosystem. PyTorch is closely associated with the people developing AI models and applications. The Cloud Native Computing Foundation (CNCF), which hosts llm-d as a sandbox project, focuses more heavily on deploying and operating systems in production. The llm-d project is a bridge between these worlds.

blocks.text: “llm-d unifies the PyTorch and CNCF ecosystems by bringing Kubernetes-native orchestration directly to vLLM and modern inference engines,” said Stephen Watt, vice president, office of the chief technology officer, Red Hat. “It delivers high-performance, distributed inference with the reliability and scale enterprises need — all within an operational model they already know.”
